doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Seeing The Man With the Golden Arm and deciding to be a drummer
summary: Goodwin recalls seeing the Sinatra film with his mother, hearing Shelly Manne on the soundtrack, and declaring himself a drummer at 14 after playing sax.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Hopefully long and profitable. A career in jazz is what I dreamed of from when I was about 11 years old, even before I knew what I was dreaming about, and it came together in a strange way. While viewing a movie with my mother, “The Man With the Golden Arm” with Frank Sinatra. If you know the story then you know I don’t have to explain it. And it featured — I’d been getting into music, west coast jazz particularly. I had certain favorites and they were all in this movie. At some point there was a big band scene, Sinatra was playing it. Sinatra was a family friend you know. I grew up in Hollywood and my father was in show biz and my mom was too and they were friends of Sinatras who lived in our neighborhood. Well anyway, he had had a hard time going after his big scandal with Ava Gardner. Anyway my mom, she really liked Frank and so she took us to see his movie. And he was very good in it, playing the former junkie drummer who just gets out of jail and decides he wants to be a drummer. It’s a Nelson Algren novel, quite, you know like you know Walk on the Wild Side — that guy. So I was struck by the music and seeing, hearing Shelly Manne on the soundtrack and I just thought to myself, my 12-year-old self, I can do that. I could play the drums. I know exactly what he’s doing.
You were playing the saxophone at the time, weren’t you.

I was playing sax, yeah, but I was never a good sax player. I could play, I could read music and I could play in the school bands, and I continued that through junior high and high school. I played saxophone and I played drums, depending on the situation. But when I went to the first year of high school I was 14, in the ninth grade and I declared myself a drummer. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
